column4: hull-euler: sec:chain-core "For a compatible metric on $X$, a point $x$ is \emph{chain recurrent} if, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there are $r\ge1$ and $x=x_0,x_1,\dots,x_r=x$ with $d(Tx_i,x_{i+1})<\varepsilon$." IsMetricChainRecurrent is the printed definition. It agrees with the entourage definition, and on compact X it does not depend on the compatible metric. LANDED 20911e5b2
hull-euler: sec:chain-core "Write $Y=\operatorname{CR}(T)$ for the chain-recurrent set." On compact X the set does not depend on the compatible uniformity. LANDED 20911e5b2

hull-euler: sec:chain-core "We first construct this set in a form that also supplies finite ring models." This sentence announces the plan. The ring-model construction is chain-core S3, the retained subshift. LANDED 20911e5b2

hull-euler: lem:chain-core-models "The set $Y$ is nonempty, closed and invariant, and $R_Y$ is LEF." Covers the closed and invariant parts. By the lead's ruling 09-13 16:20, nonemptiness comes from chain-subshift's coreSubshift_nonempty and fff-quotient's coreSubshift_eq_chainRecurrentSet; the second is on main (b34b97bfe), the first was not at 17:00. LEF of $R_Y$ is chain-core's. LANDED 20911e5b2

hull-euler: lem:chain-core-models "The complement $X\setminus Y$ is covered by translates of sets $P\setminus T(P)$, where $P$ is clopen and $T(P)\subseteq P$." Closed endpoint over compact Hausdorff totally disconnected X. The proof is the atom-graph argument (lead's ruling 09-13 16:20). LANDED 5b63c946c

hull-euler: lem:chain-core-models "Each of these sets is wandering: its distinct integer translates are pairwise disjoint." IsWandering is the printed definition. The closed endpoint carries wandering of every P \ T(P) with T(P) ⊆ P. LANDED 20911e5b2 5b63c946c

hull-euler: proof of lem:chain-core-models "These defects are wandering by nesting of the translates of $P$." Nesting: T^(k+1)(P) ⊆ T(P), so distinct integer translates of P \ T(P) are disjoint. LANDED 20911e5b2 5b63c946c

hull-euler: proof of lem:chain-core-models "Chain recurrence passes to factors, so $Y\subseteq Y_*$." Covers the first clause, for a continuous semiconjugacy over compact X. The inclusion $Y\subseteq Y_*$ for the itinerary factor is not yet applied on main. LANDED 20911e5b2
